To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the problem of computing a minimum-width cover for a set of points by k strips can be solved efficiently in two dimensions, but is NP-hard in three or higher dimensions; (b) the same problem for slabs can be solved efficiently even in three dimensions; and (c) the problem of finding a cover for a set S ⊂ Rd using d-cylinders can be solved efficiently for any fixed dimension d.
for any fixed d ≥ 2, we can compute a cover of a set of n points in Rdd by O(k logk) slabs or d-cylinders, each of width or diameter at most 2w* in expected polynomial time.

for d = 2 we can compute a cover of the input points by O(k log2k) strips of width w* in time O(nk2 log4n), and for d = 3 we can compute a similar cover by O(klog2k) slabs of the same width in time O(n3 log4n).
